summary:
Región de Los Lagos stands under Chile's national framework for gender identity, non-discrimination, hate-crime aggravation and partner recognition. Those provisions apply in the region on the same terms as elsewhere in the country and are set out in the national record. No Los Lagos-specific statute, court ruling, police directive, health protocol or care restriction was identified in the sources reviewed.

The region-specific signal is Movilh's XXIV annual report (HECHOS 2025, published March 2026), which records Los Lagos as accounting for 3.14% of the 3,620 cases and complaints of discrimination documented nationally in 2025, the fourth-largest regional share, with a 9.09% year-on-year increase recorded for the region. The report reads the national pattern as documented hostility expanding into regions with less public debate, and that is the frame in which the Los Lagos share is presented.

The 3.14% figure is a share of nationally documented cases, not a per-capita rate, and the report supplies no population denominator for the regional ranking. A fourth-place rank on that basis does not by itself establish that a trans visitor or resident in Los Lagos faces a higher risk of abuse than in other regions. Documented cases also track reporting and complaint behaviour, which the report's own framing acknowledges.
tangentialFactors:
The 9.09% increase recorded for Los Lagos is smaller than the 27.1% national increase in the same reporting year, so the region's share of documented cases did not grow at the national rate. The report describes the national rise as near-universal across the country's regions rather than concentrated in one or two, which places the Los Lagos figure inside a wider pattern instead of marking the region out.

An even distribution of documented cases across the country's regions would give each region a larger share than 3.14%, so Los Lagos sits below a flat regional split. The report provides no population denominator, and the comparison is arithmetic on shares rather than a measure of individual risk.
localsOnly:
Residents of Los Lagos use the national procedures for legal gender recognition and the national non-discrimination and hate-crime framework. No regional administrative variation, regional health protocol or regional identity-document procedure was identified in the sources reviewed.

The regional figures in the annual report are drawn from cases and complaints documented nationally, so reports made by Los Lagos residents feed the region's count. The report's regional table is the only division-level breakdown located for the region.
outOfScopeNotes:
Outright International's Chile dossier, published 12 March 2026, contains no division-specific legal, incident or enforcement finding for Los Lagos. Its content is national and is carried by the national record.

The 2025 edition of the annual report does not reproduce the 2024 regional share, so no comparison of Los Lagos's own share across the two editions is possible. No population or per-capita denominator for the regional ranking was located, and no Los Lagos-specific prosecution, police action or incident was identified in the sources reviewed.
